newsitem.title: CHINA: China vows to resist foreign tobacco companies.
newsitem.headline: China vows to resist foreign tobacco companies.

text.p: Beijing will mount a full-scale defence against foreign tobacco companies that use massive advertising to try to shift their cigarette markets to China, the Xinhua news agency said Saturday.
China aimed eventually to launch a nationwide ban on cigarette advertising, the official agency quoted Vice Minister of Public Health Cao Ronggui as saying at a conference on smoking and health.
In recent years, Western tobacco firms had spent huge sums on advertising in an attempt to transfer their cigarette consumer markets to China, Cao said.
"China will by no means allow such a thing, and will resist the trend with all-out efforts," Xinhua quoted him as saying.
International tobacco companies have said China's huge and growing army of around 300 million smokers make it an important alternative to increasingly health-conscious Western markets.

China's health authorities have made repeated efforts to avert what some experts see as a looming health crisis for the nation's cigarette smokers, but laws aimed at curbing smoking and cigarette advertising have proved difficult to enforce.
The ultimate aim of regulations on tobacco promotion issued by major cities was to wipe out cigarette advertising throughout the country, Xinhua quoted Cao as saying, but gave no timescale.
